scope: The class of the content unit that a source represents. It is not the file extension, the transport, the quality of the copy, the rights class or the intended use.

classes.definition: A book or an independently identifiable book volume, with an evidenced bibliographic identity and an authorial or editorial structure.
classes.boundary: An ISBN or a page count is not a required test. A verified fragment of a book keeps the book identity, and its partial coverage is stated in the result.

classes.definition: A standalone article, preprint, or research or technical report that addresses a bounded subject as its own publication.
classes.boundary: Length and peer-review status do not by themselves make a source a book, and a paper's class proves nothing about its claims.

classes.definition: A contextual archive of an application, a workspace or a correspondence, treated as that archive: its records, their order, participants, relationships and state are retained.
classes.boundary: Saving a book or a paper out of an application does not make the saved file an export.

classes.definition: A standalone structured collection of observations, examples or records with a data schema or a dataset description.
classes.boundary: A table exported from a database with described columns can be a dataset; tables inside a paper do not change the paper's class.

classes.definition: A source of a recognised type that lies outside the four classes above.
classes.boundary: An invoice or a slide deck can be other. A source that is unreadable or whose type is uncertain is not other: it is unknown or ambiguous.

statuses.class: exactly one of the five class ids

statuses.candidates: at least two distinct classes other than other

separate_vocabularies: Knowledge Contract role, skill, competency, blueprint, constraint and work-item kinds
the document types of the publication catalogue

migration.history: kc-doc-class/0 existed only as a proposal in correspondence between project agents and in a task description. No classification result, receipt or other data was ever written with it.
migration.rule: A /1 classification is a new artefact for the same source key. A changed version label does not re-evaluate a source, earlier records are kept, and an unknown taxonomy identifier or a canon digest that does not match is refused instead of being read as the latest canon.
